title: Coupling between expected pairs and collision probability

problemStatement.formal: probCollision n d \le \uparrow(\text{expectedPairs}\ n\ d)\ \wedge\ \text{probCollision}\ n\ d \ge \frac{(\text{expectedPairs}\ n\ d)^2}{E[X^2]}
problemStatement.plain: Bracket the Birthday Problem collision probability between (i) the Markov upper bound C(n,2)/d = expectedPairs n d (OQ01) and (ii) the Paley-Zygmund lower bound E[X]^2 / E[X^2]. Sandwiches OQ02's product-formulation probCollision between OQ01's first-moment quantity above and a second-moment quantity below.
whyMatters: Closes a methodology gap: the gallery has both moment-based (OQ01) and probability-based (OQ02) treatments of the birthday problem, but no formal proof that the two viewpoints bracket the same quantity.
Gives variancePairs_le_expected (OQ01:164) a downstream client; currently unused without a coupling theorem.
Markov bound is sharpest at small C(n,2)/d; the OQ02 exponential bound is sharpest near the threshold; the two couplings together produce a complementary pair of closed-form bounds.
Mathlib has no Finset.one_sub_prod_le_sum lemma at the pinned revision; a gallery-side proof has upstream value.

proven: one_sub_exp_neg_ge_div_one_add: private bridge for the lower bound.

insights: The current bracket is independent of OQ01 and does not require the descFactorial bridge.

The descFactorial bridge is a clean ~22-line proof: rewrite each (1 - i/d) as (d-i)/d (using i < k ≤ d so the Nat subtraction does not truncate), split with Finset.prod_div_distrib, then chain Nat.cast_prod with Nat.descFactorial_eq_prod_range.
The S6 ACT proof avoids induction entirely; all steps are Mathlib name lookups.

S8 PREP: birthday indicators I_{ij} are pairwise UNCORRELATED (not independent) — both shared-element and disjoint cross-pairs give E[I·I'] = 1/d², equal to the product of marginals. Hence Var(X) = sum of Var(I_{ij}) with zero cross-covariance, simplifying E[X²] to a clean closed form.
mathlibGaps: A tighter second-moment proof may still need local probability algebra rather than a direct Mathlib API.
